items.prompt: In a parallel-line diagram, angle 3 and angle 6 are alternate. If angle 3=68°, find angle 6 and the co-interior angle 5.
items.reasoning: Alternate angles are equal; co-interior angles sum to 180°.

items.prompt: A triangle has angles 35° and 85°. Find the third angle and classify the triangle.
items.reasoning: 180−35−85; all angles are acute and different.

items.prompt: Name the polygons with 5, 6 and 8 sides.
items.reasoning: Polygon names count sides.

items.prompt: Which construction locates all points equally distant from A and B? A) angle bisector B) perpendicular bisector C) parallel line D) circle centre A.
items.reasoning: The perpendicular bisector is the locus of points equidistant from A and B.

items.prompt: Use the parallel-line diagram. Find a, b and c.
items.reasoning: Corresponding and alternate angles are equal; co-interior angles sum to 180°.

items.prompt: The angles of a triangle are x, 2x and 3x. Find x and classify the triangle.
Find each base angle x.
items.reasoning: (180−40)÷2; base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal.

items.prompt: An exterior angle of a triangle is 115°. One opposite interior angle is 48°. Find the other opposite interior angle and the adjacent interior angle.
Complete the table: quadrilateral → __ triangles, __°; pentagon → __ triangles, __°; hexagon → __ triangles, __°.
items.reasoning: An n-gon splits into n−2 triangles; multiply by 180°.

items.prompt: A regular polygon has exterior angle 45°. Find the number of sides and each interior angle.

Order the steps for a perpendicular bisector of AB=8 cm: (i) draw arcs from A and B with the same radius; (ii) draw AB; (iii) join the arc intersections; (iv) open the compass to more than half of AB. State the radius condition.
items.answer: ii, iv, i, iii; radius >4 cm.
items.reasoning: The arcs must meet; the line through the intersections is perpendicular and bisects AB.

items.prompt: Test whether these triples can form a triangle: 3,4,8; 5,5,9; 6,7,10.
items.reasoning: Compare the sum of the two shorter sides with the longest.

items.prompt: A ramp makes 12° with the ground. What angle does it make with a vertical post?
items.reasoning: Ground and vertical are perpendicular: 90−12.

items.prompt: The truss has equal base angles of 65°. Find the apex angle, the exterior angle at a base, and classify the triangle.
items.reasoning: 180−65−65; 180−65; equal base angles imply equal rafters.

items.prompt: A scale drawing uses 1:20. The model base is 30 cm. Find the real base in metres.
A path must pass through points equally distant from gates A and B. Which construction locates the path? Explain.
items.reasoning: Every point on the perpendicular bisector is equidistant from A and B.

items.prompt: A collar is parallel to the base. At a rafter joint it makes a 66° co-interior angle. Find the angle on the other side of the collar at that joint.
items.reasoning: Co-interior angles sum to 180°.

items.prompt: The kite is made from two congruent triangles. One triangle has angles 40° and 70°. Find the missing angle and explain why the matching angle in the other triangle is equal.
items.answer: 70°; corresponding angles of congruent triangles are equal.
items.reasoning: 180−40−70; congruence preserves angles.

items.prompt: A student says a triangle with sides 4 cm, 4 cm and 9 cm is possible because 4+9>4. Correct the reasoning.
items.answer: Impossible: the two shorter sides give 4+4<9.
items.reasoning: The triangle inequality must be checked using the two shorter sides against the longest.

items.prompt: Can a triangle have two obtuse angles? Explain.
items.reasoning: Two obtuse angles already sum to more than 180°.

items.prompt: True or false: any two angles between parallel lines are equal. Justify.
items.reasoning: Corresponding and alternate angles are equal; co-interior angles are supplementary.

items.prompt: A student says the exterior angle 110° should be added to the opposite interior angles 60° and 50° to make 180°. Identify the error and correct it.
items.answer: The exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles: 110°=60°+50°. It is not added to them to make 180°.
items.reasoning: The adjacent interior angle is 70°; 110° and 70° are supplementary.

items.prompt: Complete the missing steps: a heptagon has __ sides, splits into __ triangles, so its interior angle sum is __.
A student uses a compass radius of 2 cm to bisect a 6 cm segment. The arcs do not meet. Explain why and state a suitable radius.
items.answer: The radius must be greater than half of 6 cm, so greater than 3 cm; 2 cm is too small.
items.reasoning: Equal-radius arcs meet only when the radius exceeds half the segment.

items.prompt: Use the arcs to explain why sides 5 cm, 8 cm and 13 cm do not form a triangle.
items.answer: They form a degenerate straight line because 5+8=13.
items.reasoning: Equality gives zero area; the two shorter sides must exceed the longest.

items.prompt: Why should construction arcs be kept visible?
items.answer: They record the equal radii and the defining property, so the construction can be checked.
items.reasoning: A construction is an argument made with instruments.

items.prompt: Two sides of a triangle are 7 cm and 11 cm. The third side is a whole number of centimetres. Find all possible values.
Construct an isosceles triangle with equal sides 6 cm and base 8 cm. Explain why the perpendicular bisector of the base passes through the apex.
items.answer: The apex is equidistant from the base endpoints, so it lies on the perpendicular bisector.
items.reasoning: Equal sides place the apex on the locus of points equidistant from the endpoints.

items.prompt: A regular polygon has each interior angle five times its exterior angle. Find the number of sides.
items.reasoning: Interior + exterior =180°; 6e=180°, e=30°, n=360÷30.

items.prompt: A truss has an 8 m base and equal rafters of length x m. Find the smallest whole-number value of x that makes a triangle.
items.reasoning: 2x>8, so x>4; x=4 gives a degenerate straight line.

items.prompt: Use compass arcs to explain why the two shorter sides of a triangle must together exceed the longest side.
items.answer: If the base is the longest side c, arcs of radius a and b from the endpoints meet above the base only when a+b>c. If a+b=c they meet on the base; if a+b<c they do not meet.
items.reasoning: The arc intersection is the possible apex; no intersection means no triangle.
